subject: Banking
title: The Debt Spiral
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Debt Spiral usable.

hook.text: Americans carry $17.3 trillion in total debt. When interest payments consume income, the spiral toward default begins.

buildup.text: Debt spirals start small. One missed payment raises the interest rate.

discovery.text: Credit card penalty rates jump to 29-30% after one late payment. The punishment makes recovery almost impossible.

twist.text: Debt stress causes health problems. Studies show it increases heart disease, depression, and anxiety.

climax.text: Debt spirals are self-reinforcing. Higher rates cause more missed payments, which cause higher rates.

punchline.text: One missed payment. Higher rate. More missed payments. The spiral accelerates.

quiz.question: What triggers a debt spiral?
options: Missed payments raising rates, making future payments harder

details.summary: A debt spiral occurs when borrowers take on new debt to pay existing obligations, each loan carrying higher interest than the last. The compounding interest creates an accelerating cycle that becomes mathematically impossible to escape without intervention.
details.whyItMatters: Debt spirals destroy financial lives and are by design hard to stop once they start. Understanding the mechanics helps people recognize the warning signs early and take action before the spiral becomes irreversible.
takeaways: New debt at higher rates to pay old debt accelerates the cycle
Minimum payments barely cover interest, preventing principal reduction
Intervention through counseling, consolidation, or bankruptcy may be needed

faq.question: What are the warning signs of a debt spiral?
faq.answer: Using credit cards to pay bills, taking cash advances, missing minimum payments, borrowing from payday lenders, and feeling impossible stress about money. If new debt is consistently needed to cover existing obligations, the spiral has begun.

faq.question: How do you escape a debt spiral?
faq.answer: Stop borrowing immediately, even if it means difficult lifestyle changes. Seek free credit counseling. Explore debt consolidation at lower rates. Consider balance transfer offers. In severe cases, bankruptcy provides a legal fresh start.
